name: MESSENGER
best_known_for: First Mercury orbiter — used 6 planetary gravity assists (1 Earth, 2 Venus, 3 Mercury) over 6.6 years to bleed energy before orbit insertion in 2011, then mapped the planet for 4 years before impacting the surface in 2015
credit: Discovery-class Mercury Surface, Space ENvironment, GEochemistry, and Ranging mission. Launched on a Delta II 7925H-9.5 with a Star-48B kick stage on 2004-08-03. The 6.6-year cruise used 6 gravity assists (Earth 2005-08, Venus 2006-10 + 2007-06, Mercury 2008-01 + 2008-10 + 2009-09) to lose ~5 km/s of heliocentric energy — direct Mercury orbit insertion would have required impossible delta-v. Mercury orbit insertion 2011-03-18 at 12:45 UTC; original 12-hour 200 × 15 200 km orbit later trimmed to 8-hour 200 × 10 300 km. Mission discoveries: water ice in permanently shadowed polar craters, organic-rich dark material at the poles, exosphere composition, magnetic-field offset from planet centre, abundant hollow-bottomed pits suggesting volatile loss. Impacted Mercury 2015-04-30 after exhausting propellant; left an artificial 16 m crater near the north pole.

links.l: Solomon et al. (2018) — Mercury: The View After MESSENGER (Cambridge Press)
